read_only.instructions: Graphersal dev server: an in-memory property graph (Gremlin/TinkerPop model: vertices and edges with labels and properties) that a user works with LIVE in a browser playground at the same time; the browser reloads when you change the graph. Prefer GQL, the ISO graph query language (it also accepts the Cypher spellings, such as CREATE and UNWIND), for reading and writing data: the `gql` tool takes the query text as it is (MATCH ... WHERE ... RETURN, rows as JSON objects, INSERT / CREATE, SET, REMOVE, DELETE and MERGE writes; experimental, see its description). Use `query` for what GQL does not cover: Gremlin (Apache TinkerPop) in Rhai syntax, and scripts with several statements (see its description). Use `get_schema`/`statistics`/`graph_info` to learn the data first, and the schema tools to read or evolve the schema. Before writing a new query, check `list_saved_queries`: saved queries are named, parameterized queries the user stored in the graph, each written in GQL (`language: "gql"`) or in Gremlin (Rhai); run one with `run_saved_query` {name, params} instead of writing it again (a GQL query calls one written in GQL as `CALL folder.name(args) YIELD col`). Saved queries marked `writes: true` change data (their `effects` say what); run them only when the user asked for that change. Large text that queries rarely read (CVs, descriptions) can be kept compressed in memory with a compression rule: `list_compressions`, `estimate_compression` (measures the candidate rules on the current data first, changes nothing), `define_compression`, `drop_compression`, `recompress` (reads stay plain); `memory_report` shows where the memory goes per label and property, `workload_statistics` which queries ran and how the properties were used. A query that filters a label on a property (`g.v().has_label("person").has("age", P.gt(30))`) and is slow on a large graph can be served by a property index: `list_indexes`, `create_index` {label, key, element?, type?, transform?}, `drop_index`; results never change, `.profile()` names the index it reads. For a case-insensitive search create it with transform "to_lower" and query `has("name", __.to_lower().is("alice"))` (the constant compared as given, so write it in lower case). Resources: graphersal://dsl-reference (every step and function), graphersal://examples (runnable examples), graphersal://saved-queries, graphersal://schema, graphersal://statistics. To create test data, use `Fake(seed)` inside a query (reproducible English names, e-mails, addresses, companies and random numbers; section "Test data generator" of graphersal://dsl-reference, group "Generated test data (Fake)" of graphersal://examples). Every query is one transaction: a failing query changes nothing. Errors carry a `Help:` line that names the fix. Answers are compact JSON. `query`, `gql` and `run_saved_query` page their results: at most `max_rows` results (default 100) after the first `offset` ones (default 0), `max_items` items of every nested list (default 100), and only whole results within the server's answer limit (`graph_info`: `answerLimitChars`); a trailing note says what was shown and names the next page's `offset`. Bound large answers in the query itself (LIMIT, `values(..)`) or page them. Persistence (checkpoints, history, views of past states) is the user's, in the browser: when the user opens a read-only view of a past state, `graph_info` says so and writes are refused until they go back to the live graph. This server is READ-ONLY for MCP: only reading tools are offered and a query that would write is refused.

tools.description: Run a Graphersal script: Gremlin in Rhai syntax (double-quoted strings, `__.` for child traversals, tokens such as P.gt(30), Order.desc, T.label); statements end with `;`, the last value is the result, and a traversal before it runs only with a terminal (.to_list(), .next(), .iterate()). Compact JSON, paged (offset, max_rows, max_items). Prefer the gql tool for plain reads; in a script GQL is g.gql("MATCH ...", #{name: value}) and a saved query g.query("name", #{..}). Every step: resource graphersal://dsl-reference. Example: g.v().has_label("person").values("name")

tools.description: Where the memory goes per label and property (bytes, types, compression, indexes) and per process component; changes nothing.

limit.description: Keep the property rows and the label rows with the most bytes (default 50 each).

max_elements.description: Sample so that about this many elements are read, at least one per label (default: all).

max_labels.description: Keep the label rows with the most bytes (default: limit); labels_omitted counts the rest.

max_rows.description: Keep the property rows with the most bytes (default: limit); rows_omitted counts the rest.

scope.description: all (default): every element the graph shows; delta: only a layered graph's own elements, its base as shared_bytes (the whole graph for a plain one).
